This drain pump works well and it fixed the minor leak under my washing machine. On the basis of just its looks, it is not as complex in its construction as the original Kenmore pump it replaced after 24 years of faithful service. On the other hand, it appears to be made entirely of plastic, which is probably a good thing since it won’t rust like the original did. Due to rust on the metal part of the pump’s outlet fitting, it took 3 hours to remove the Kenmore pump! I had to totally destroy the original pump to remove it! Even if this pump only lasts a few years, it should be much easier to replace, and it’s inexpensive.

Was pleasantly surprised to find out we can still buy parts for old machines to keep them going.  The pump arrived in only a couple days and only cost a few bucks (especially compared to the cost of a new washer).  The hardest part was removing the old/leaky one and cleaning up the shaft of the motor with a wire brush in a drill.  After about 30 yrs of operation, the old pump kind of bonded to the motor.  But once the motor was cleaned up, this new one fit perfectly and drains the washer even faster than before.  The question now is if I'll get another 30 yrs out of this pump.....

Then had leak ! Sent back installed another one. Leaked again. Inspected and found leak originated from dent in spout where mold either put part number or mold construction.
Original did not have these dents. Good news is leak stopped after three days. I guess rubber filled dent under pressure from clamp. So inspect yours. I put automotive hose clamps on to stop leak.

I am sure glad I took the leap and purchased this pump replacement, the manufacturer pump went out and was leaking, lucklie I have my washer outside cause of past experiences with leaky machines. I'll update if it quits before a couple year's.
